_about: Field terms for F109, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

sampling-lattice.definition: a regular arrangement of points at which a continuous signal is measured; square, hexagonal, cubic and body-centred cubic are examples, and each can represent signals up to a limit of fineness set by its geometry
sampling-lattice.excludes: irregular or adaptive sample placements, and the pixel shape of a display

aliasing.definition: the error made when a signal holds detail finer than the samples can represent, so that the fine detail is rebuilt as false coarse detail
aliasing.excludes: noise in the measurement, and blur from the rebuilding filter

bcc.definition: the cubic lattice with one more point at the centre of every cube; the face-centred cubic lattice instead adds a point at the centre of every face, and each of the two is the reciprocal of the other
bcc.excludes: a claim about any material's crystal structure

geodesic-grid.definition: a set of points on a sphere made by subdividing the faces of an icosahedron and pushing the points out to the surface; each point has six near-equal neighbours except twelve that have five, so the layout is close to hexagonal everywhere
geodesic-grid.excludes: a latitude-longitude grid, whose points crowd together at the poles

psnr.definition: peak signal-to-noise ratio, a measure in decibels of how closely a rebuilt image matches the original; higher is closer, and 1 dB is a change of about 21 percent in mean squared error
psnr.excludes: a measure of how good the image looks to a viewer

gabor-frame.definition: a set of copies of one short window, shifted in time and in frequency onto a lattice of points, such that any signal can be rebuilt stably from how strongly it matches each copy
gabor-frame.excludes: a basis; a frame has more members than strictly needed, by a factor called the redundancy

frame-condition.definition: the ratio B/A of a frame's upper and lower bounds, which says how much rebuilding can amplify errors in the coefficients; 1 is ideal
frame-condition.excludes: a measure of how few coefficients a signal needs

benjamini-hochberg.definition: an adjustment of a set of p values that holds the expected share of false discoveries among the results called significant at a chosen level
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: a guarantee that no result in the set is a false discovery
